name: Herbalist
summary: A Universal World Class any character may take regardless of their class. It levels through active use — foraging, harvesting and crafting — unlocking tools, methods and higher tiers of ingredient, from woodland herbs to planar flora and monster parts.
_thresholds_note: Mastery to reach levels 2, 3, 4 and 5. The author's table read 10/25/50/100; the top two are kept and the bottom two raised, because 10 and 25 did not reach the author's own stated pacing. A qualifying level-1 craft is worth about 5 MP (3 first-time, +2 for a second stage), so 10 MP is two crafts against a target of 3-5; a level-2 craft is about 9 MP, so 25 is under three against a target of 6-8. At 25 and 65 those become 5 and 7.  The DIP AT LEVEL 4 IS DELIBERATE — do not 'fix' it. The author's craft counts fall from 6-8 to 4-5 at that step because each high-tier recipe is a larger undertaking, and 50 MP is 4.5 crafts at 11 MP each, which is exactly the target.
_deeds_note: The deed for Herbalist 5 was 'crafting a legendary catalyst', and read literally that gate could never open: `catalyst crafting` is a Level 5 method and legendary material is Level 5 material, so the deed required the level it was gating. Measured by brute force over every method permutation an Herbalist 1-4 knows against every legendary ingredient: 0 legal chains. Level 5 was unreachable and so was every catalyst. The deed is therefore the material, not the method — successfully working legendary material is the grand catalyst, and `catalyst crafting` is the mastery that follows it. An Herbalist 4 reaches legendary material the one way the rules already allow: the concentration ladder, two exotic doses into one legendary one, at 15%.

legendary-catalyst.note: Any successful craft at legendary tier, however it was reached.

levels.note: Basic poultices, teas and crushed powders.
Field harvesting of monster parts and delicate flora.
Concentration of liquids into potent tinctures, oils and tonics.
Safe handling of hazardous, toxic or planar substances.
Masterwork concoctions, permanent elixirs and maximum efficiency.

method_descriptions.grind: Pulverises solid ingredients into fine powders, preparing them for poultices, additives or inhalants.
method_descriptions.mix: Combines two distinct ingredients. The mixture keeps the primary effects of both at 80% of base strength and duration.
method_descriptions.brew: Steeps or boils ingredients in liquid to create teas, broths and washes. Unlocks full duration and secondary effects for liquid remedies.
method_descriptions.preserve: Waxes, drying or solvents to extend the shelf life of perishable ingredients.
method_descriptions.extract: Harvests organ meats, venoms and delicate plant nodes without destroying their magical properties.
method_descriptions.distill: Concentrates a liquid mixture: +25% to the primary effect, or turns a raw ingredient into an indefinite tincture.
method_descriptions.purify: Removes negative side effects, penalties and secondary toxicities while keeping the beneficial traits.
method_descriptions.infuse: Imbues liquids or powders with planar energy or monster essence, combining up to three components into one dose.
method_descriptions.neutralize: Disarms contact toxins and environmental side effects during harvesting.
method_descriptions.refine: Raises a crafted item to 125% of base strength, or extends its duration by 50%.
method_descriptions.catalyst crafting: Uses legendary components to craft permanent stat-altering elixirs and grand alchemical catalysts.

_portable_note: The workbench is furniture. Whether a recipe can be attempted is therefore partly a question about where the character is standing, which is scene state rather than sheet state.
_fixed_tools_note: Declared and deliberately unread. Ruled 2026-08-25: leave these alone until property ownership exists. An immovable installation only means anything once a character can own, buy and place one — at which point these become the things you purchase and site, and the bench asks where you are standing. Until then the workbench folds out wherever the character is, which is the recorded design call, and gating on a building nobody can own would only refuse work.
